public_rationale: The dated record of people completing the Boston Marathon establishes that humans were alive on April 15, 2024. That settles the narrow observation. Survival on that date does not contradict a prediction about extinction at an unspecified future time.
limitations: This assesses neither future AI risk nor Marcus’s characterization of Yudkowsky’s position.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: So far, AI has not killed humanity as Yudkowsky warned.

statement.excerpt: Eliezer Yudkowsky warned that AI was (inevitably!) going to kill us all. I am happy to report that so far it hasn’t.
statement.document_title: TED, AI, and the test of time

our_interpretation: Assess only Marcus’s observation that humanity had not been killed by AI by April 15, 2024.
The existence of living humans on that date is sufficient to establish that human extinction had not occurred.
This does not adjudicate the accuracy of his paraphrase of Yudkowsky or any prediction about later extinction.
So far limits the observation in time; it is not a conditional forecast antecedent.
criteria.support_condition: A reliable dated record establishes that at least one human was alive on April 15, 2024.
criteria.contradiction_condition: AI had caused the death of every human by that date.
